Materials

[RESEARCH IDEA]
## Problem Statement
Deep learning approaches to Multiview Structure from Motion (SfM), particularly those utilizing matrix equivariant architectures for projective factorization, have shown theoretical promise. However, these methods currently rely on a brittle assumption: that the input point tracks are nearly free of outliers. In real-world scenarios—such as large collections of internet photos—feature tracking heuristics inevitably introduce erroneous matches (outliers). Existing deep factorization networks lack the mechanism to filter these errors, causing them to fail catastrophically when applied to realistic, noisy data. There is currently no effective deep equivariant framework capable of simultaneously cleaning the data and recovering 3D structure from uncurated image collections.

## Core Hypothesis
We hypothesize that the geometric consistency required for SfM can be learned as a pattern recognition task within the equivariant latent space. By integrating an explicit inlier/outlier classification module directly into the equivariant architecture, the network should be able to identify observations that violate the collective motion consensus of the scene. If we can successfully predict and mask these outliers *before* or *during* the factorization process, the deep network will be able to recover accurate camera poses and 3D structures even from highly contaminated inputs, effectively performing a "learned RANSAC" within a deep learning framework.

## Proposed Methodology (High-Level Technical Approach)

We propose a multi-stage pipeline that purifies the input data via deep learning before solving for geometry.

**1. Equivariant Feature Encoding**
We will construct a neural encoder designed to process the input point-track tensor (a sparse matrix of 2D observations). Crucially, this encoder will enforce permutation equivariance with respect to both cameras (rows) and scene points (columns). This ensures that the network focuses on the geometric relationships between views and points rather than their arbitrary ordering. The output will be a high-dimensional latent representation of the track matrix.

**2. The Outlier Classification Module**
Instead of immediately regressing pose, we will introduce a dedicated classification head operating on the latent features. This module will evaluate each entry in the track tensor to determine its probability of being an outlier. By leveraging the equivariant structure, the classifier will assess the consistency of a specific point's motion relative to other points in the same track and other tracks in the same image.

**3. Geometry Regression Heads**
Parallel to the outlier detection, we will utilize specific regression heads to predict the camera parameters (rotation and translation) and the 3D coordinates of the scene points. These heads will aggregate features along the relevant dimensions (pooling across points to find camera pose, and across cameras to find point locations).

**4. Inference Strategy: Purification and Robust Refinement**
Our inference process will mimic a "clean-then-solve" logic:
*   **Purification:** We will first run the network to predict an outlier mask.
*   **Fine-tuning:** We will apply this mask to the input data and fine-tune the network on the specific scene to minimize reprojection error using only the predicted inliers.
*   **Robust Bundle Adjustment:** Finally, we will implement a specialized post-processing optimization. Unlike standard bundle adjustment, this step will iteratively filter out points with high reprojection errors or low visibility, effectively pruning the reconstruction graph to ensure sub-pixel accuracy and geometric stability.

## Expected Contribution
*   **Robustness in Deep SfM:** We expect to demonstrate that deep projective factorization can be made robust to heavy outlier contamination, moving beyond the limitation of "clean data only."
*   **Cross-Scene Generalization:** By training the outlier detector on diverse data, we aim to create a model that generalizes across different datasets and scene types without scene-specific retraining for the classification task.
*   **Bridging the Gap:** This work aims to elevate deep SfM methods to a level of practicality comparable to classical robust pipelines, enabling the processing of uncontrolled, large-scale internet photo collections.

[EXPERIMENTAL LOGS]
## 1. Experimental Setup

We designed and executed a comprehensive evaluation of a deep equivariant Structure from Motion (SfM) network that integrates an inlier/outlier classification module and a robust Bundle Adjustment (BA) scheme. The experiments were designed to test robustness against outliers in point tracks across various realistic and synthetic datasets.

*   **Datasets Used:**
    *   **MegaDepth:** 196 outdoor scenes. Divided into two groups: Group 1 (< 1000 images) and Group 2 (> 1000 images).
        *   *Training Set:* 27 scenes from Group 1.
        *   *Validation Set:* 4 scenes from Group 1.
        *   *Test Set:* 14 scenes from Group 1 and subsampled versions (300 images) of scenes from Group 2.
    *   **1DSFM:** Used for cross-dataset generalization testing. Diverse urban scenes.
    *   **Strecha:** Small dataset ($\le 30$ images) with ground truth LIDAR data. Used for cross-dataset generalization.
    *   **BlendedMVS:** Synthetic dataset with ground truth camera poses.

*   **Data Preprocessing (Point Tracks):**
    *   Extracted SIFT features for all images.
    *   Applied exhaustive pair-wise RANSAC matching.
    *   Chained sequences of two-view matches to create point tracks.
    *   Discarded points viewed in fewer than 3 cameras or containing inconsistent cycles.
    *   *Note:* Input point tracks contained significant outliers (up to ~47% in some test scenes).

*   **Ground Truth Generation:**
    *   For MegaDepth and 1DSFM (which lack native ground truth), we utilized COLMAP reconstructions applied directly to the scene images to establish pseudo-ground truth for camera poses and structure.
    *   For Strecha and BlendedMVS, we used the provided ground truth.

*   **Evaluation Metrics:**
    *   **Camera Rotation Error:** Angular difference in degrees between predicted and ground truth orientation (Mean and Median).
    *   **Camera Translation Error:** Difference between predicted and ground truth locations (Mean and Median).
    *   **Number of Registered Cameras ($N_r$):** The count of cameras successfully recovered in the reconstruction.
    *   **Runtime:** Inference time, fine-tuning time, and bundle adjustment time.
    *   **Classification Metrics:** Recall (inliers/outliers), Precision (outliers), F-score (outliers).

*   **Baselines Compared:**
    *   **ESFM:** Equivariant SfM (Deep-based). Evaluated on original contaminated tracks and "clean" tracks (denoted ESFM*).
    *   **GASFM:** Graph Attention SfM (Deep-based).
    *   **Theia:** Global SfM pipeline (Classical).
    *   **GLOMAP:** Global SfM pipeline (Classical).
    *   **VGGSfM:** Differentiable end-to-end SfM (Deep-based).
    *   **MASt3R:** Pairwise pointmap prediction merging (Deep-based).
    *   **COLMAP:** Incremental SfM (Classical).

*   **Implementation Details:**
    *   **Hardware:** NVIDIA A40 GPUs (48GB memory).
    *   **Framework:** PyTorch.
    *   **Optimizer:** ADAM with normalized gradients.
    *   **Training:** Processed training scenes sequentially per epoch. Random subset of 10-20% images per scene selected during training.
    *   **Network Architecture:**
        *   Encoder: 3 layers, 256 channels, ReLU.
        *   Heads (Camera, Point, Outlier): 3 layers, 256 channels each.
    *   **Inference Procedure:**
        1.  Predict inlier/outlier scores.
        2.  Remove predicted outliers (Threshold: 0.6 for MegaDepth/1DSFM; 0.8 for Strecha/BlendedMVS).
        3.  Fine-tune network on the test scene for 1000 epochs minimizing unsupervised reprojection loss.
        4.  Apply Robust Bundle Adjustment (BA).
    *   **Robust BA Strategy:**
        *   Standard BA on predicted cameras/points.
        *   Remove points with projection error > 5 pixels or viewed in < 3 cameras.
        *   Retain largest connected component of the view graph.
        *   Triangulate remaining tracks and apply a second round of BA.

## 3. Qualitative Observations

*   **Reconstruction Visual Quality:**
    *   Observation: The proposed method produced 3D reconstructions (point clouds) that were notably cleaner than those produced by existing deep-based methods (ESFM and GASFM), particularly in the presence of high outlier ratios.
    *   Observation: Camera pose recovery (visualized as frustums) was more accurate and consistent with the scene structure compared to baselines in challenging scenes like "Piazza del Popolo" (33.1% outliers) and "Madrid Metropolis" (39.4% outliers).
    *   Observation: In scenes with fewer outliers (e.g., 0012 with 16.3%), the method still maintained robust reconstruction quality, comparable to or better than baselines.

*   **Architecture and Process Flow:**
    *   Observation: The integration of the outlier head allowed for the effective removal of erroneous matches before the fine-tuning stage.
    *   Observation: The sets-of-sets permutation equivariant architecture was validated as superior to a PointNet architecture for the specific task of classification within this SfM context.
    *   Observation: End-to-end training of the feature encoder (as opposed to freezing it) was found to be crucial for achieving high accuracy in pose estimation.

*   **Robustness:**
    *   Observation: Standard Bundle Adjustment was found to be ineffective when dealing with remaining outliers after the initial network prediction. The Robust BA protocol was necessary to achieve sub-pixel accuracy.
    *   Observation: The method demonstrated successful cross-dataset generalization, training on MegaDepth and testing on 1DSFM, Strecha, and BlendedMVS without re-training (only fine-tuning on the test scene).

*   **Limitations:**
    *   Observation: In some specific cases, the method registered fewer cameras ($N_r$) than classical methods like Theia or GLOMAP. This was attributed to the outlier removal step occasionally being too aggressive, causing the view graph to become unconnected, which forced the system to discard tracks from the disconnected components.

*   **Runtime:**
    *   Observation: The method was significantly faster than COLMAP and GLOMAP (often by a large margin in total minutes).
    *   Observation: The method was generally slower than Theia.
    *   Observation: The most time-consuming component of the proposed pipeline was the fine-tuning phase (1000 epochs per scene).

# ICLR 2025 Paper Writing Guidelines

references.text:
## Problem Statement
Multiview Structure from Motion (SfM) aims to simultaneously recover camera poses and 3D scene structure from image collections. While classical approaches rely on robust—but often slow—incremental pipelines, recent deep learning approaches utilizing matrix equivariant architectures (projective factorization) offer a promising alternative. However, a critical limitation of current deep-based projective factorization methods is their assumption that input point tracks are nearly error-free.

In realistic scenarios, such as collections of internet photos, point track extraction heuristics produce data contaminated with significant outliers due to viewpoint changes, illumination differences, and repetitive structures. Existing equivariant networks lack the mechanism to identify or reject these outliers, causing catastrophic failure in reconstruction when applied to noisy, real-world data. We need a system that retains the theoretical benefits of permutation equivariance while robustly handling contaminated inputs.

## Core Hypothesis
We propose to construct a "Robust Deep Equivariant Structure from Motion" network. Our core hypothesis is that we can extend the "sets-of-sets" permutation equivariant architecture by integrating a dedicated Multiview Inlier/Outlier Classification Module. By enforcing equivariance in the outlier detection process, the model will learn to identify erroneous matches based on their motion consistency relative to other points in the same image and within their specific track.

We further hypothesize that coupling this learnable outlier rejection with a test-time fine-tuning strategy and a specialized "Robust Bundle Adjustment" scheme will enable the deep network to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy on uncontrolled image collections, effectively bridging the gap between deep learning efficiency and classical robustness.

## Proposed Methodology (Detailed Technical Approach)

### 1. Problem Formulation
We assume a stationary scene viewed by $m$ cameras with unknown poses. The input will be a sparse point track tensor $M$ of size $m \times n \times 2$, containing 2D observations of $n$ 3D points.
*   **Cameras:** We assume internal calibration. The $i$-th camera matrix is $P_i = [R_i | \mathbf{t}_i]$, where $R_i \in SO(3)$.
*   **Structure:** We denote the $j$-th 3D scene point as $\mathbf{\bar{X}}_j \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
*   **Observations:** The entry $(M_{ij1}, M_{ij2}) \doteq \mathbf{x}_{ij}$ represents the projection of point $j$ in camera $i$. If unobserved, the entry is empty.

Our objective is to output:
1.  **Camera Matrices:** $P \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times 7}$ (Quaternion $\mathbf{q}_i \in \mathbb{R}^4$ and translation $\mathbf{t}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$).
2.  **3D Structure:** $X \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times 3}$.
3.  **Outlier Classification:** $O \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$, providing a probability score for every observation.

### 2. Network Architecture
The architecture will be equivariant to row (camera) and column (point) permutations. It will consist of four distinct modules:

**A. Permutation Equivariant Feature Encoder**
This module maps input $M \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n \times 2}$ to a latent representation in $\mathbb{R}^{m \times n \times d}$, with $d=256$. It will comprise three layers of linear equivariant maps interspersed with ReLU activations.
The linear map $L$ transforming features $\tilde{M}$ from $d$ channels to $d'$ channels is defined as:
$$ L(\tilde{M})_{ij} = W_1 \tilde{M}_{ij} + W_2 \sum_{k=1}^m \tilde{M}_{kj} + W_3 \sum_{l=1}^n \tilde{M}_{il} + W_4 \sum_{k=1}^m \sum_{l=1}^n \tilde{M}_{kl} + \mathbf{b} $$
Here, $W_1, \dots, W_4 \in \mathbb{R}^{d' \times d}$ and $\mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{R}^{d'}$ are learnable parameters. To ensure invariance to the number of observed projections, we will replace the summation operations with averages over non-empty entries.

**B. Inlier/Outlier Classification Module ($H_{outlier}$)**
Taking the latent representation $\mathbb{R}^{m \times n \times d}$ from the encoder, this module applies three Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) layers followed by a sigmoid activation.
*   **Output:** A matrix $O \in [0, 1]^{m \times n}$ representing the probability of each track point being an outlier.
*   **Equivariance:** This module maintains the input dimensions and respects equivariance, assessing point consistency within the global context.

**C. Pose Regression Head ($H_{cams}$)**
We will pool the average of the latent features along the columns (points) to obtain a representation in $\mathbb{R}^{m \times d}$. This is passed through three MLP layers.
*   **Output:** Tensor in $\mathbb{R}^{m \times 7}$ (3 values for translation, 4 for rotation quaternion).

**D. Structure Regression Head ($H_{pts}$)**
We will pool the average of features along the rows (cameras) to obtain a representation in $\mathbb{R}^{n \times d}$. This is passed through three MLP layers.
*   **Output:** Tensor in $\mathbb{R}^{n \times 3}$ representing 3D coordinates.

### 3. Loss Function
We will train the network using a combined loss function balancing supervision on outliers and unsupervised geometric consistency:
$$ \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{outliers} + \alpha \mathcal{L}_{reprojection} $$
We set the hyperparameter $\alpha = 10$.

**Outlier Loss ($\mathcal{L}_{outliers}$):**
This will be a Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) loss comparing predicted scores $O$ against pseudo-ground-truth labels derived from pre-existing reconstructions (e.g., COLMAP).

**Reprojection Loss ($\mathcal{L}_{reprojection}$):**
This term combines a standard reprojection error with a hinge loss to enforce positive depth.
$$ \mathcal{L}_{reprojection} = \frac{1}{p} \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n \xi_{ij} s_{ij} $$
Where $p$ is the total number of measurements and $\xi_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$ is the visibility indicator. The term $s_{ij}$ is defined conditionally based on the predicted depth $P_i^3 \mathbf{X}_j$:
$$ s_{ij} = \begin{cases} r_{ij}, & P_i^3 \mathbf{X}_j \geq h \\ h_{ij}, & P_i^3 \mathbf{X}_j < h \end{cases} $$
Here, $h=0.0001$ is a constant. The reprojection error $r_{ij}$ is:
$$ r_{ij} = \left\| \left( \mathbf{x}_{ij}^1 - \frac{P_i^1 \mathbf{X}_j}{P_i^3 \mathbf{X}_j}, \mathbf{x}_{ij}^2 - \frac{P_i^2 \mathbf{X}_j}{P_i^3 \mathbf{X}_j} \right) \right\| $$
And the hinge loss term is $h_{ij} = \max(0, h - P_i^3 \mathbf{X}_j)$.

### 4. Inference and Robust Bundle Adjustment
Our inference pipeline will consist of three stages:

1.  **Classification & Removal:** We run the network to predict outliers. Points with a score $O_{ij} \geq 0.6$ will be removed from the input tensor $M$.
2.  **Fine-tuning:** We will fine-tune the encoder and regression heads on the cleaned input $M$ for the specific test scene by minimizing the unsupervised $\mathcal{L}_{reprojection}$ for 1000 epochs.
3.  **Robust Bundle Adjustment (Robust BA):** Standard BA is insufficient for remaining outliers. We will implement the following procedure:
    *   Run initial Bundle Adjustment on predicted $P$ and $X$.
    *   **Filter:** Remove 3D points with reprojection error $> 5$ pixels or those viewed by $< 3$ cameras.
    *   **Connectivity Check:** If the view graph becomes unconnected, retain only the largest connected component and discard tracks from removed images.
    *   **Refinement:** Triangulate the remaining tracks and apply a second round of standard BA.

## Expected Contribution
1.  **Robustness to Realistic Data:** We aim to enable deep projective factorization on large-scale (hundreds of images) collections of uncontrolled internet photos, a domain where previous equivariant methods fail.
2.  **Learnable Outlier Rejection:** By integrating the outlier module directly into the equivariant framework, we provide a theoretical contribution regarding how to learn geometric consistency in a permutation-invariant feature space.
3.  **Cross-Scene Generalization:** The trainable architecture is designed to generalize across different scenes and datasets without retraining, requiring only test-time fine-tuning.

preinstalled.zh: 编排镜像：上游代码（固定提交、未改）、uv 锁定依赖、docker CLI（经 shim 给兄弟容器加代理和 CA）；agent 镜像：上游自己的 agent-cli Dockerfile
preinstalled.en: orchestrator image: upstream code at the pin (unmodified), uv-locked dependencies, the docker CLI (a shim adds proxy and CA to sibling containers); agent image: upstream's own agent-cli Dockerfile

notes.benchmark_paths: A benchmark item's paths are mounted into the agent containers unless upstream mounts the same path itself (/workspace and below, /home/agent-home, /task-source, /run, /tmp): those are left out and listed in logs/sibling-mounts.txt. The agents work in upstream's own /workspace (the run directory), so a deliverable the official prompt names under such a path is not written where the run collects it.
notes.venue: paper.paper_format=iclr for every task. The system has only iclr and alife specs and does not choose a venue itself; ICML and NeurIPS templates and a system-chosen venue are unsupported.
notes.task_input: Only the `# Goal` and `# Rubrics` sections of task.md are read: all five candidate files are put under `# Goal` with their headings turned into bold lines; `# Rubrics` carries a neutral line. The paradigm is optimisation of a scalar score: the task-drafting phase (documented as experimental) turns the brief into an evaluator and a seed program.
notes.phases: execution.phases=task_drafting,investigation,final_evaluation,paper; the system's own default also runs ablations and posthoc; final_evaluation stays because a drafted task requires it before the paper. review/revision (second model) are never selected.
notes.agent_pool: agent.pool and agent.models.* are left empty: one model for every phase.
notes.second_provider: No OPENAI/GEMINI key is supplied (concept figures stay in deterministic export mode).
notes.time: No global wall-clock or token cap exists upstream; the runner enforces time_limit_hours. Native caps used: idea cycles=3, per-phase timeouts from [systems.agentic-scientist].
notes.network: Sibling agent containers run on the shield's internal network; the agents keep their CLI WebFetch/Bash network, which go through the shield. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield.
notes.search: Provider server-side web search is switched off in every sibling by the agent CLIs' own system settings, bind-mounted read-only by the docker shim: Claude Code /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (permissions.deny WebSearch), Codex /etc/codex/config.toml (web_search="disabled") and /etc/codex/requirements.toml (allowed_web_search_modes=["disabled"]). Upstream's own Semantic Scholar client goes through the shield.
notes.key_exposure: The provider key is in the environment of the agent containers (upstream env-file mechanism) and therefore visible to commands the agent runs. Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 was tried and aborts: it needs bubblewrap, which the unmodified upstream agent image lacks.
notes.gpu: gpus=1 is wired (container.gpu_count, harness GPU evaluation) but was not exercised.
notes.docker_socket: The orchestrator container has the host docker socket (root-equivalent on the host).

preinstalled.zh: python:3.11 bookworm；上游代码按 PYTHONPATH 使用；pdflatex + bibtex；CPU 版 PyTorch 和 numpy、scipy、scikit-learn、pandas、matplotlib 等（constraints.txt 固定）
preinstalled.en: python:3.11 bookworm; upstream code via PYTHONPATH; pdflatex + bibtex; CPU PyTorch with numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, matplotlib and more (pinned by constraints.txt)

notes.model: claude-opus-5-5 through the Anthropic Messages API (llm.provider=anthropic), no fallback models, reviewer model = same model. Requests carry model, messages and max_tokens only (no tools, no thinking parameter); ARC's per-stage temperature is not sent because the model rejects it, so the API default applies.
notes.agent: ARC is not a tool-using coding agent: its 23-stage pipeline, its own code agent and its reviewers are prompt chains over plain chat completions. conditions.agent=claude means only that the provider is Anthropic; Claude Code is not involved. Generated experiments run as a plain subprocess in the container.
notes.effort: ARC has no effort setting; usage-log.patch sends output_config.effort='high' with every request. Haiku 5.5 thinks by default and ARC's per-stage max_tokens (for example 4096) is shared with the thinking tokens, so long outputs can still be cut short.
notes.venue: Not chosen by the system: export.target_conference=iclr_2026 comes from [systems.autoresearchclaw].
notes.tokens: ARC records no usage. A logging-only patch (usage-log.patch) appends each Messages API `usage` block to anthropic-usage.jsonl; cost is not computed. The same patch carries the RWE_OMIT_TEMPERATURE and RWE_EFFORT switches.
notes.time: No global wall-clock or budget cap in ARC; only the runner's limit applies. Per experiment run 3600 s, refinement iterations 10, repair cycles 3.
notes.input: Chinese pack text goes verbatim (candidate files concatenated, with <!-- file --> markers) into prompts.extra_prompts of 18 stages. ARC takes one topic string and checks generated code against it, so research.topic is the candidate TASK.md verbatim with whitespace collapsed. Literature queries come from the stage-3 model plan; ARC's ASCII keyword splitter and its whitespace-based query expansion yield a few useless queries from the Chinese text. Starter papers are guidance text only: ARC cannot ingest seed papers.
notes.search: Web search, crawling, GitHub, HF Hub, Gemini and OpenCode are off. Literature search in stage 4 uses ['openalex', 'semantic_scholar'] through ARC's own clients behind the shield proxy; stages 8, 17, 22 and 23 (novelty, citation verification) always also query arXiv, CrossRef and DataCite; the shield date-bounds those API calls like the others (a late DOI answers 403).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: every request to api.anthropic.com is built in researchclaw/llm/anthropic_adapter.py:136-148 and carries only model, messages, max_tokens, optional temperature, output_config.effort and system, never a tools or web_search field; the OpenAI-compatible client (OpenRouter :online / plugins) is not used (llm.provider=anthropic), web_search.enabled=false, Gemini is only used by the disabled figure_agent.nano_banana. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so such a path would be invisible to the audit.
notes.secrets: Generated experiment code inherits the container environment, including the API keys (ARC offers no switch to scrub it).
notes.profile: project.profile=ml_generic is fixed for all tasks; research.domains is left empty because the literature screen rejects papers outside the stated domain (a theory task failed with domains=[machine-learning]).

preinstalled.zh: 上游锁定依赖（uv sync --frozen）加兼容补丁 compat.patch；TeX Live（含 fonts-extra、latexmk）；给 agent 用的研究 Python 环境 /opt/research
preinstalled.en: upstream's locked dependencies (uv sync --frozen) plus compat.patch; TeX Live (with fonts-extra and latexmk); a research Python environment for the agent in /opt/research

notes.agent: No external coding agent: EvoScientist runs its own in-process planner/research/code/debug/writing sub-agents (LangChain deepagents) on the one configured model. conditions.agent only selects the provider; Claude Code and Codex are not used.
notes.model: Main agent, sub-agents and EvoScientist's auxiliary calls (tool selector, memory workers, summariser, graders) all use the configured model; auxiliary_model and model_fallbacks are empty.
notes.effort: Upstream hard-wires effort=max and max_tokens=128000 for Anthropic models. compat.patch makes the effort come from EVOSCIENTIST_REASONING_EFFORT (= conditions.effort); max_tokens stays 128000 (a cap, not a cost driver). Adaptive thinking (display=summarized) is upstream and not switchable.
notes.paper: The core writes a Markdown report (final_report.md); the EvoSkills paper-writing skill gives a generic LaTeX `article` skeleton with no ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS style and no compile step. The image has TeX Live (latexmk, fonts-extra) but no venue style files; the task asks for an official template, so a venue-formatted PDF depends on the agent obtaining the style through the shield. No extra pipeline stage was added; absent items are listed in result.missing.
notes.tools: skill_manager (git clone of any repository as a skill) is not registered (compat.patch); the Tavily key is not set so tavily_search does not exist; LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1; EvoSkills is baked in at its pinned commit. The execute shell and the EvoSkills paper-navigator scripts reach the world only through the shield; S2_DATE_CUTOFF is not set (the shield bounds dates).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: EvoScientist binds no provider-side search tool to any model (its only tools are think_tool, tavily_search when TAVILY_API_KEY is set, MCP tools from mcp.yaml, deepagents built-ins and skills; EvoScientist/EvoScientist.py:671-672 and 754-755 at the pin; the one bind_tools call is the tool selector's own output schema, middleware/tool_selector.py:166). TAVILY_API_KEY is not passed and the image has no mcp.yaml, so no search tool exists. Anthropic/OpenAI hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so a provider-side search would be invisible to the audit.

notes.agent: No external coding agent: EvoScientist runs its own in-process planner/research/code/debug/writing sub-agents (LangChain deepagents) on the one configured model. conditions.agent only selects the provider; Claude Code and Codex are not used.
notes.model: Main agent, sub-agents and EvoScientist's auxiliary calls (tool selector, memory workers, summariser, graders) all use the configured model; auxiliary_model and model_fallbacks are empty.
notes.effort: Upstream hard-wires effort=max and max_tokens=128000 for Anthropic models. compat.patch makes the effort come from EVOSCIENTIST_REASONING_EFFORT (= conditions.effort); max_tokens stays 128000 (a cap, not a cost driver). Adaptive thinking (display=summarized) is upstream and not switchable.
notes.paper: The core writes a Markdown report (final_report.md); the EvoSkills paper-writing skill gives a generic LaTeX `article` skeleton with no ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS style and no compile step. The image has TeX Live (latexmk, fonts-extra) but no venue style files; the task asks for an official template, so a venue-formatted PDF depends on the agent obtaining the style through the shield. No extra pipeline stage was added; absent items are listed in result.missing.
notes.tools: skill_manager (git clone of any repository as a skill) is not registered (compat.patch); the Tavily key is not set so tavily_search does not exist; LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1; EvoSkills is baked in at its pinned commit. The execute shell and the EvoSkills paper-navigator scripts reach the world only through the shield; S2_DATE_CUTOFF is not set (the shield bounds dates).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: EvoScientist binds no provider-side search tool to any model (its only tools are think_tool, tavily_search when TAVILY_API_KEY is set, MCP tools from mcp.yaml, deepagents built-ins and skills; EvoScientist/EvoScientist.py:671-672 and 754-755 at the pin; the one bind_tools call is the tool selector's own output schema, middleware/tool_selector.py:166). TAVILY_API_KEY is not passed and the image has no mcp.yaml, so no search tool exists. Anthropic/OpenAI hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so a provider-side search would be invisible to the audit.
